articles.title: Who is Verity Ockenden? Inside the UK 10-mile defending champion’s career, achievements, personal life and more
articles.summary: Verity Ockenden is a British middle- and long-distance runner who competes for Swansea Harriers.
articles.body: Verity Ockenden is a British middle- and long-distance runner who competes for Swansea Harriers. The 35-year-old athlete has built a strong reputation on the track and roads. She won the UK 10-mile title at the 2025 Great South Run and will return to Portsmouth on October 18, 2026, to defend her crown.Ockenden has also represented Great Britain internationally. One of the biggest achievements of her career came at the 2021 European Athletics Indoor Championships, where she won bronze in the women’s 3000m. She has continued to compete at a high level and has enjoyed another strong season on the roads.Who is Verity Ockenden?Born on August 31, 1991, Verity Ockenden developed into an accomplished distance runner. She represents Swansea Harriers AC and has competed across several distances during her career.Ockenden made her mark internationally at the 2021 European Athletics Indoor Championships in Toruń, Poland. She won the bronze medal in the women’s 3000m event. The result remains one of the biggest achievements of her career with Great Britain.She has also established herself as a strong competitor in domestic road races.Ockenden won the UK 10-mile title at the 2025 Great South Run. She completed the race in 56:37. It was particularly significant because she had previously finished second and third in earlier editions of the event.She is now set to return to Portsmouth for the 2026 edition of the Great South Run. Ockenden will face a strong women’s field, including debutant Izzy Fry.Fry won the British 10,000m title in Loughborough in May before competing at the Commonwealth Games. Other runners in the field include Daisy Glover, Esme Davies, Hannah Irwin, Holly Archer, Natasha Philips and Cassie Thorp.Ockenden is hoping to defend her title against the strong competition.“The Great South Run has always been special for me as a race that ties together family history in Portsmouth, my coach Chris Thompson’s legacy here, as well as marking a lot of turning points in my own career,” said Ockenden. “It’s a real honour to be able to return to defend my title and I’ll be bringing my best effort in order to retain it.”Her 2025 victory was not her only impressive result on the roads. She also enjoyed a strong campaign at the Great Manchester Run, where she won silver in the UK 10km road championships and finished fourth overall.Ockenden has recorded impressive personal bests across different distances. Her indoor 3000m best stands at 8:46.60, while she has run 8:43.87 outdoors. Her 5000m personal best is 15:03.51.Away from competitive running, Ockenden has several interests and talents. She studied English and Italian at Swansea University and has developed a career as a writer and poet. She has also contributed regular columns to Athletics Weekly.Her creative work often connects running with nature and movement. She has written about forest running and the way natural surroundings influence her poetry.Ockenden has also worked as a professional chef. articles.title: 2nd Test weather forecast at Gqeberha: Day-by-day rain chances for SA vs AUS at St. George's Park
articles.summary: SA vs AUS 2nd Test weather forecast: Check day-by-day rain chances, cloud cover, and hourly radar for St George's Park in Gqeberha after Day 1 rain delays.
articles.body:
Australia star Scott Boland took two wickets in two balls before rain left South Africa on 20-2.

Rain is likely on Monday, but Gqeberha should clear up from Tuesday onwards.

Officials can add 30 minutes and bring start times forward to recover lost overs.

South Africa vs Australia 2nd Test: Scott Boland replaces Nathan Lyon, strikes twice early in Gqeberha

The weather forecast for the second Test at Gqeberha points to another damp morning before conditions improve, and the rain chances at St George's Park will shape how much cricket Australia and South Africa can actually play over the next four days.

Australia won the toss and asked South Africa to bat, but the covers came back on as soon as the coin had been flipped, following overnight rain. Play did not begin until two hours after the scheduled start, and the hosts were 11-0 when the rain interrupted again and an early lunch was taken.

Australia fast bowler Scott Boland took two wickets with consecutive deliveries on a rain-hit opening day on Sunday, and South Africa were 20-2 when stumps were called early.

Boland was the only change to the Australian XI after the side's 214-run win in the first Test in Durban, and he bowled opener Aiden Markram for 11 before dismissing David Bedingham for a golden duck with the very next ball, as the batter edged a delivery into the gloves of wicketkeeper Alex Carey.

Debutant Marques Ackerman was on 5 and captain Temba Bavuma on 4 when rain stopped play around 40 minutes after lunch. The showers refused to ease, and the umpires called stumps one hour and 45 minutes before the scheduled close.

Gqeberha weather forecast for the 2nd Test: Day-by-day rain chances

Heavy rain and overcast skies ruled the day, with a high of 19°C, a low of 13°C and an 85 per cent chance of precipitation. Persistent coastal drizzle caused several interruptions, and early stumps were called. Chance of rain: Very high

Cloudy skies are expected with thundershowers in the morning and breezy winds off the coast, with temperatures between 11°C and 18°C. The chance of rain is put at 75 to 80 per cent, so a delayed start is very likely, although a resumption after lunch is possible. Chance of rain: High

Conditions should clear partially, with sunny intervals and a few passing clouds. Temperatures will range from 12°C to 21°C, and the rain probability falls to 10 to 15 per cent. A full day of play is expected, and the match officials are likely to schedule make-up overs. Chance of rain: Low

An overcast morning should give way to a bright and breezy afternoon, with a high of 23°C and a low of 14°C. The chance of rain is around 10 per cent, so play should be uninterrupted, and batting is expected to become easier under the sun. Chance of rain: Low

The final day looks mostly dry with late sunny spells and a moderate south-westerly breeze, with temperatures between 14°C and 20°C. The rain probability is only 5 to 10 per cent, and the pitch is likely to deteriorate, which could bring reverse swing into play. Chance of rain: Very low

How the coastal low-pressure system and green pitch will affect play at Gqeberha

The first 36 to 48 hours of the Test are being controlled by a cold coastal low-pressure front that is moving off the Indian Ocean across Algoa Bay. The system caused Sunday's near washout, and forecasters expect lingering dampness through Monday morning before it moves eastwards out to sea by Tuesday.

The curators left plenty of grass on the strip to help the seamers, and humidity of more than 90 per cent, along with moisture trapped under the covers for long periods, should add to the effect. Boland, Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood are therefore likely to extract exaggerated sideways movement and steep bounce each time play restarts.

How match officials can recover lost overs in the Australia vs South Africa Test

The officials have the option of adding up to 30 minutes, which is roughly eight overs, at the end of each remaining day. They can also bring the start time forward to 9:30 AM local time, or 1:00 PM IST, to make up for the 77.4 overs lost on day one.

Will rain affect the 2nd Test between South Africa and Australia?

The opening two days are likely to be badly hit by showers, but the weather should improve considerably from Tuesday, and full days of play are expected over the final three days.

Australia remain favourites, but the lost overs could decide the Test

Australia hold a strong hand after day one, even though only 12.2 overs were bowled. Scott Boland's two quick wickets have given the visitors a psychological edge, and the green pitch, heavy air and covers that stayed on for hours will keep the seamers interested whenever play resumes. Having won the opening Test in Durban by 214 runs, the tourists will also feel that time is on their side if they can force a result before the weather turns again.

However, South Africa should not be written off. Debutant Marques Ackerman has already shown some patience, and Temba Bavuma remains at the crease, so a recovery is possible if they survive the early moisture. The forecast suggests that batting will become much easier from Tuesday, which could reward a side that stays patient through Monday's gloom.

The bigger question is whether five days will be enough. With 77.4 overs lost, the match officials will need to use every extra minute, and a draw cannot be ruled out. Still, Australia's four-man seam attack suits the conditions better, and they remain favourites, provided that at least three full days of play are possible.

articles.title: Bryce Young's TD pass gives Panthers 10-0 lead over Eagles
articles.summary: The Eagles are struggling without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts.
articles.body:
The Eagles are struggling without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts.

They trail the Panthers 10-0 with 8:08 remaining in the second quarter.

Bryce Young hit tight end Tommy Tremble for a 12-yard score, completing a five-play, 35-yard drive. Eagles punter Braden Mann's 23-yard punt set up the Panthers with good field position.

They faced a second-and-20 after an intentional grounding penalty on Young, but got a first down on the next play when Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis was called for roughing the passer.

The Panthers have outgained the Eagles 143 to 74, with Young going 9-of-16 for 128 yards and a touchdown.

articles.title: Rashod Bateman exits Ravens-Browns game with shoulder injury
articles.summary: Rashod Bateman is listed as questionable to return against Cleveland with a shoulder injury after missing practice time this week
articles.body:
Baltimore's passing game has another injury concern after Rashod Bateman exited Sunday's matchup against the Cleveland Browns with a shoulder injury. The Ravens wide receiver is listed as questionable to return.

Bateman entered the AFC North matchup after dealing with a shoulder issue during the practice week. He missed Thursday's session, returned to full participation Friday, and entered Sunday without an injury designation.

His exit leaves Baltimore awaiting another update on a receiver who was cleared to play but now faces uncertainty about finishing the game. The Ravens are already operating without Lamar Jackson, with Tyler Huntley starting again while Jackson recovers from an ankle injury.

Bateman's availability bears watching beyond Sunday, given the shoulder issue's impact on his preparation for Cleveland. If he cannot return, Baltimore will need its remaining receivers and tight ends to absorb his opportunities as Huntley tries to keep the offense moving against a division opponent.

articles.title: Selby out but Lisowski advances in NI Open defence
articles.summary: Reigning champion Jack Lisowski begins his defence of the Northern Ireland Open with a 4-1 victory over Huang Jiahao in Belfast, but Mark Selby makes a surpr...
articles.body:
Reigning champion Jack Lisowski began his defence of the Northern Ireland Open with a 4-1 victory over Huang Jiahao in Belfast, but Mark Selby made a surprise first-round exit.

Lisowski, 35, won his first ranking title at the tournament last year and raced into a three-frame lead over his Chinese opponent at the Waterfront Hall.

The Englishman allowed Jiahao to cut the deficit to 3-1 but would clinch the fifth frame on the black to advance.

He will now face Scotland's Anthony McGill, who enjoyed a 4-1 victory of his own over Stephen Maguire, in round two.

While Lisowski ensured safe passage into the second round, there were surprises on the opening day of the tournament with Selby and Xiao Guodong both beaten in round one.

Four-time world champion Selby was hoping to become the first player to win the quartet of Home Nations tournaments, but was beaten 4-2 by Louis Heathcote.

The world number five, who has already won the China Open this year, led 2-0 but dropped four straight frames to exit.

Xiao Guodong, meanwhile, lost a final-frame decider to England's Sam Craigie and Cork's Aaron Hill was also beaten in the first round with a 4-2 defeat by Thailand's Thepchaiya Un-Nooh.

Former world champions Neil Robertson and Shaun Murphy are among those in action during Sunday's evening session, which begun at 19:00 BST.

articles.title: Florida leaps back into AP Poll's top 25 after Week 7 upset win
articles.summary: An upset win on the road over Texas in Week 7 has Florida football back in the AP Poll's top 25, cracking the top 20 in their return to the rankings.
articles.body:
Florida football snapped its two-game skid on Saturday with a huge win in Austin over Texas — the program's first-ever victory on the Longhorns' home turf and first top-10 road win since 2012.

The offense looked solid with Tramell Jones Jr. under center in his first collegiate start and the defense showed resilience that had been lacking in previous outings. Jon Sumrall's squad had just enough moxie to pull things off after a late rally by the home team.

After falling out of the AP Top 25 last week, the Gators find themselves back in the mix at No. 20 with 355 points, putting them between No. 19 Texas (440) and No. 21 Boise State (295).

Florida is joined by eight fellow SEC schools in the rankings after Week 7, led by fifth-ranked Georgia, followed by Ole Miss (No. 7), Tennessee (No. 11), Kentucky (No. 12), Alabama (No. 13), LSU (No. 18), Texas (No. 19), Florida (No. 20) and Missouri (No. 22). Auburn and Mississippi State also appeared on the ballot with 61 and 52 points, respectively.

The Gators also made their way back into the US LBM Coaches Poll top 25 and now sit at No. 24.

Next up, Florida has a bye week before facing Georgia in the annual rivalry game on Saturday, Oct. 31. That game will be played in Atlanta and broadcast on ABC starting at 3:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Ravens in control, lead Browns 10-0 at halftime
articles.summary: Baltimore’s defense has dominated Cleveland’s offense through two quarters, with the Ravens leading 10-0 at halftime.
articles.body:
Baltimore's defense has dominated Cleveland's offense through two quarters, with the Ravens leading 10-0 at halftime.

Starting for the second week in a row for the injured Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley capped Baltimore's first possession with a 2-yard touchdown pass to rookie tight end Josh Cuevas.

Tyler Loop then ended Baltimore's second drive with a 34-yard field goal to give his team a 10-point advantage.

Huntley is 14-of-21 for 107 yards with a touchdown at halftime. He's also rushed three times for 22 yards.

Derrick Henry — who became the fourth player in league history to rush for 4,000 yards with two teams — has rushed for 41 yards on 11 attempts.

The Browns had just one first down and 7 total yards at the end of the first quarter. They were able to get a couple more in the second quarter, but still finished with just 46 total yards.

Deshaun Watson is 3-of-9 passing for 24 yards. He's looked uncomfortable in the pocket, holding onto the ball before getting hit or sacked, with Baltimore bringing him down three times in the first half.

Jerry Jeudy has two of Watson's completions for 23 yards.

Notably, Baltimore receiver Rashod Bateman is questionable to return with a shoulder injury.

Browns safety Grant Delpit is out due to a concussion.

Cleveland will receive the second-half kickoff.

articles.title: Kevin Durant, Mat Ishbia trade shots as Dillon Brooks responds to ‘DUI’ jab
articles.summary: PHOENIX — Former Phoenix Suns star Kevin Durant and Suns owner Mat Ishbia traded shots online Saturday, revisiting Durant’s short — and, for some, polarizing...
articles.body:
PHOENIX — Former Phoenix Suns star Kevin Durant and Suns owner Mat Ishbia traded shots online Saturday, revisiting Durant's short — and, for some, polarizing — time in the Valley.

Aug 16, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Phoenix Mercury owner Mat Ishbia in attendance of the game against the Portland Fire at Mortgage Matchup Center. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images

The exchange began after Ishbia reflected on the Suns' 2023 blockbuster trade for Durant during an interview with CNBC Sport. Ishbia said he initially "threw money at the problem" and acknowledged that adding star talent doesn't always lead to championships.

Durant, a 16-time All-Star, responded on X, taking issue with the suggestion that the trade represented a failed approach. He also wrote that Ishbia seemingly came after him as if he had been arrested for a DUI — a remark many interpreted as a jab at Suns forward Dillon Brooks.

"#blameKD even though KD stayed on top of his game at 36 and got u back this 'culture' you love so much," Durant wrote.

Ishbia responded, writing that Durant had misunderstood the interview.

"You obviously didn't watch the clip," Ishbia wrote. "Didn't blame you @Kdtrey5, but am happy with the culture we are building here in Phoenix."

In another post , Durant wrote that Ishbia should be thankful he didn't have to pay him "an absurd amount of money to play for another team." While most of the exchange unfolded on X, Brooks took his thoughts to Instagram.

Apr 7, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant (7) against the Phoenix Suns at Mortgage Matchup Center. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images

Brooks, who joined the Suns in the trade that sent Durant to Houston before the 2025-26 season, wrote on an Instagram story , "Thanks Matt for cleaning up that stench in the locker room before I came #culture."

Durant's earlier reference to a DUI appeared to be a reference to Brooks' arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence in Scottsdale in March, and he later faced charges stemming from the incident.

Apr 7, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant (7) argues with Phoenix Suns forward Dillon Brooks (3) in the first half at Mortgage Matchup Center. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images

The exchange highlights the lingering tensions surrounding Phoenix's decision to acquire Durant and its subsequent move to trade him. Fans continue to debate whether Durant brought the Suns closer to a championship or simply failed to fit the mold the franchise envisioned when it made the blockbuster deal.

Now, with the Suns and Rockets scheduled to meet twice this season — Nov. 7, Nov. 25, and Feb. 5, 2027 — the online feud adds another layer of intrigue to an already anticipated matchup.

articles.title: The eye-watering price Knicks fans will have to pay for courtside seats at home opener vs LeBron James’ 76ers
articles.summary: The New York Knicks’ opening night game against the Philadelphia 76ers is arguably the most anticipated matchup at Madison Square Garden in the last few deca...
articles.body:
The New York Knicks' opening night game against the Philadelphia 76ers is arguably the most anticipated matchup at Madison Square Garden in the last few decades.

It's not just because of the exciting game the Knicks are expected to have against LeBron James' new team, but on opening night, the Knicks are set to get their championship rings, and the banner will be raised to the rafters for the first time in 53 years.

Jalen Brunson, who led the Knicks to the championship, already envisioned the ring night during the team's preseason game against the Toronto Raptors.

While he will be excited for the memorable night, fans will have to pay a premium if they want to be part of the celebrations at Madison Square Garden.

New York Knicks ring night tickets priced at over $20,000

Undoubtedly, the Knicks vs. 76ers game is always going to be a popular matchup, as both of these teams are contenders in the Eastern Conference.

Prices to get into the game on Tuesday are extremely high, with the most expensive ticket priced at $20,148, according to StubHub . This ticket is courtside and would definitely give a closer view of the ceremony.

While there are tickets priced between $2,000 and over $8,000, the cheapest one is priced at $1,072.

Prices to get into Madison Square Garden for the playoffs were also extremely expensive. However, that did not stop fans from storming into the arena to support the Knicks throughout the postseason.

It is certain that some of the biggest stars in Hollywood will be present at the Garden. With tickets still available, fans will try their best to make their way into the arena, but the prices of tickets definitely make things a little challenging for them.

According to StubHub, the Knicks are the most in-demand team in the league. This means prices to get into the Garden are expected to be high throughout the 2026-27 season.

articles.title: Miami is No. 1 in AP Top 25 for 1st time since ’02, No. 2 BYU’s ranking best since ’84 title season
articles.summary: The wildest and wackiest week of the college football season so far saw five of the top seven teams lose — a first in the AP poll’s 90-year history.
articles.body:
Miami is No. 1 in The Associated Press Top 25 for the first time since 2002, No. 2 BYU has its highest ranking since its 1984 national championship season and Notre Dame and Georgia stayed in the top five Sunday after both lost close games.

The wildest and wackiest week of the college football season so far saw five of the top seven teams lose — a first in the AP poll's 90-year history. Miami and BYU were the biggest beneficiaries of the chaos and were joined by Ohio State in a tightly bunched top three.

Week 7 of the college football season was one for the ages, where five of the top eight teams in the Week 6 AP poll lost, and three SEC powerhouses dropped games in upset fashion.

The Hurricanes took over the top spot from Georgia, which lasted one week at No. 1 after losing to Auburn at home. The Bulldogs were the second No. 1 team in two weeks — Texas was the other — to lose to an unranked opponent.

Miami survived end-of-game drama to beat rival Florida State in double overtime and stay unbeaten. The Hurricanes' two-spot jump made them No. 1 for the first time since the 2002 season ended in the national championship game against Ohio State.

The Hurricanes received 40 of the 70 first-place votes from the media voting panel and were just 22 points ahead of BYU, which won a thriller at home over Notre Dame. The Cougars got 20 first-place votes and were 26 points ahead of Ohio State. The Buckeyes got nine first-place votes and were well ahead of No. 4 Notre Dame and No. 5 Georgia.

Miami is the first No. 1 team from the Atlantic Coast Conference team since Clemson in 2020. Other than Clemson, there had not been another ACC team ranked No. 1 since Florida State in 2014.

BYU went into its game against Notre Dame as a 10.5-point underdog and came out with a 28-24 win to go 6-0 for a third straight year. Since their championship season 42 years ago, the Cougars hadn't been higher than No. 4 in a poll or in the top five since 1996.

Every single spot in the Top 25 has a new team this week, but only two teams dropped out of the rankings. A wholesale shakeup of the top 10 did not happen largely because Notre Dame, Georgia and No. 6 Indiana had built-up capital with their 6-0 starts, plus the losses by the Fighting Irish and Hoosiers were against top-10 opponents.

Indiana, which lost at home to Ohio State , was followed by Mississippi, Texas Tech, UCLA and Utah. Texas Tech received the remaining first-place vote.

Alabama's loss at Tennessee dropped the Crimson Tide seven spots to No. 13 and Texas plummeted 12 rungs to No. 19 after its home loss to Florida.

In and out In: No. 20 Florida, which dropped out last week after consecutive lopsided losses, is back after going to Texas and handing the Longhorns a second loss in a row.

In: No. 25 Arizona, which had an open date, has four straight double-digit wins since losing to BYU and makes its season debut in the poll.

Out: Oklahoma State's loss at Houston brought an end to the Cowboys' three-week run in the poll.

Out: Mississippi State got bounced for the 31-0 loss at LSU that followed a 23-point home loss to Alabama.

The last time the SEC's top team in the rankings — it's No. 5 Georgia this week — was behind teams from each of the other power conferences was Dec. 3, 2023, when Alabama was No. 5 behind teams from the Big Ten (Michigan), Pac-12 (Washington), Big 12 (Texas) and ACC (Florida State).

The last time the Nos. 1 and 2 teams lost in the same week in the regular season was 2017, when No. 1 Alabama lost to Auburn and No. 2 Miami lost to Pittsburgh on Thanksgiving weekend.

The last time unranked teams knocked off No. 1s in consecutive weeks was 1990. Miami hosts unranked Pittsburgh on Saturday.

No. 9 UCLA has matched its highest ranking since 2022 and No. 14 Houston has its highest ranking since it was No. 11 at midseason in 2016.

SEC (9 ranked teams): No. 5 Georgia, No. 7 Mississippi, No. 11 Tennessee, No. 12 Kentucky, No. 13 Alabama, No. 18 LSU, No. 19 Texas, No. 20 Florida, No. 22 Missouri.

Big Ten (5): No. 3 Ohio State, No. 9 UCLA, No. 15 Iowa, No. 16 USC, No. 24 Northwestern.

Big 12 (5): No. 2 BYU, No. 8 Texas Tech, No. 10 Utah, No. 14 Houston, No. 25 Arizona.

ACC (3): No. 1 Miami, No. 17 Wake Forest, No. 23 SMU/

No. 7 Mississippi at No. 19 Texas: The Rebels have found their footing after that 24-point loss to Florida, outscoring Vanderbilt and Missouri by a combined 83-20. Longhorns are reeling and might have a new QB this week.

No. 14 Houston at No. 10 Utah: The Cougars have beaten one ranked team each of the last three seasons and will go for a second against an unbeaten Utah team that escaped Colorado as a 15.5-point favorite.

articles.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. stats in Houston Texans debut
articles.summary: Marvin Harrison Jr. made his debut with the Houston Texans. How did he do?
articles.body:
Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. made his Houston Texans debut on Sunday in London. The Texans beat the Jacksonville Jaguars 34-31 on a last-second 49-yard field goal Ka'imi Fairbairn after the Jaguars had tied the game with a 60-yard field goal.

A week after Harrison was traded from the Arizona Cardinals to the Texans, many fans likely are interested in his performance.

How did Marvin Harrison Jr. play for Texans?

Harrison had a limited role in his debut, playing 12 snaps for the Texans. He lined up on the boundary nine times and in the slot three times.

In those 12 snaps, he was targeted four times. He had three catches for 34 yards. His first catch, a 14-yard reception, was his long. Here is the play:

Three catches for 34 yards is nothing to write home about, but it did come in only 12 snaps. By comparison, his best game this season with the Cardinals was in Week 2 when he caught three passes for 40 yards on five targets in Week 3 against the San Francisco 49ers. However, he was on the field for 66 snaps.

Assuming his role increases in the weeks to come, it appears his usage will be more than it was for the Cardinals this season.

He had five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown in four games. He was inactive last week for the Cardinals. He was dealt to the Texans on Sunday with a sixth-round pick in 2027 in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick and 2027 seventh-round pick.

articles.title: Northampton beat Cardiff for first English win
articles.summary: Northampton edge to a nervy Champions Cup pool win against tenacious Cardiff at Franklin's Gardens.
articles.body:
Tries: Pater, Thame, Hendy, Dingwall Cons: Belleau 3, Pater

Northampton became the only English side to win in the opening round of the Champions Cup by battling past Cardiff.

Saints, quarter-finalists last season, scored four tries at Franklin's Gardens in a nervy Pool Four encounter.

The English champions led 14-0 at half-time thanks to efforts in tricky conditions by James Pater and Toby Thame.

Tenacious Cardiff struck back through Harri Millard and Mason Grady to make it a two-point game in the final quarter.

But George Hendy and Fraser Dingwall responded as Northampton got off to a winning start, albeit without a bonus point.

Northampton's success came at the end of a chastening opening weekend of the top-tier tournament for Prem clubs, with Gloucester drawing against champions Bordeaux-Begles but six other sides losing.

Cardiff's return to the top tier of Europe after two seasons in the Challenge Cup was a considerable one.

Saints had scored 24 tries in their three opening fixtures of their Prem title defence, including 11 against Bath last time out at Franklin's Gardens.

The Welsh side also had to contend with a five-day turnaround to a United Rugby Championship (URC) fixture against Sharks at Cardiff Arms Park.

That led to several influential players being held back, although they did give first appearances of the season to Wales and Lions internationals Taulupe Faletau and Josh Adams after injury.

Northampton also made changes because of a big fixture on the horizon - the short trip to Leicester on Saturday - but got the job done.

Full-back Pater opened the scoring for Saints with a supporting run and centre Thame crashed over after 20 minutes.

Both Northampton number eight Callum Chick and Cardiff lock Tom Manz knocked on going for the line as slippery conditions led to it being 14-0 at half-time.

The Blue and Blacks struck back early in the second half when centre Millard hit a nice line in the 22 and then defended stoutly to frustrate their hosts, forcing them into a raft of handling errors.

It was 14-12 on the hour when, after Saints fly-half Anthony Belleau was sin-binned for a breakdown offence, the ball was floated to the right by Jarrod Evans for Grady to cross.

Cardiff scented an upset only for Hendy to respond swiftly, juggling the ball for a try that Pater converted.

The Northampton wing went from scoring five points to saving them by chasing down Adams when a try seemed certain.

Dingwall dashed over in the 78th minute but the hosts could not find the fifth try that was needed for a five-point haul.

Saints travel to Stade Francais in December and return to France in January to face Montpellier before a home finish to the group stage against Bulls.

Cardiff host Bath in December and then face a pair of French teams in January, travelling to Stade Francais and entertaining Montpellier.

articles.title: Carson Steele injury: Eagles RB injured against Panthers [UPDATE]
articles.summary: The Eagles RB depth got even thinner early in Week 6 against the Panthers.
articles.body:
The Eagles running back depth is already thin, to but it lightly, but things appeared to get worse in the first quarter on Sunday against the Panthers. Carson Steele nabbed a short pass by Tanner McKee, was pushed out of bounds, and was injured on the play. After a short evaluation in the medical tent, Steele headed to the locker room, and was later ruled questionable to return due to a shoulder injury.

Steele did return to the sideline with his helmet, and later in the second quarter was able to get back on the field with the special teams unit. It didn't last long, however, and after helping with kickoff duties, he was back in the medical tent for what looked like the same shoulder injury.

The RB was signed to the active roster just over a week ago, and played in London against the Jaguars, although all of his snaps came on special teams. Steele was getting some offensive opportunities early in Week 6 against the Panthers, and was targeted twice, hauling in one catch for four yards — the play on which he was injured.

The Eagles running back room is already without Saquon Barkley due to injury, and both Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley were put on IR, leaving Dameon Pierce as the starting RB, Steele, and then Jaydon Blue, as the only other active rushers.

articles.title: Real Madrid mandará ayuda a Colombia por víctimas de terremoto tras reunión con Álvaro Uribe
articles.summary: En un encuentro de alto perfil que conecta la diplomacia social, el liderazgo político y el deporte de élite mundial, el expresidente de Colombia, Álvaro Uribe Vélez, se reunió en España con Florentino Pérez, presidente del Real Madrid. La cita tuvo como propósito central articular alianzas de cooperación internacional enfocadas en la atención a las víctimas del reciente terremoto en Colombia y en el impulso de proyectos de desarrollo social para las poblaciones más vulnerables.
articles.body: En un encuentro de alto perfil que conecta la diplomacia social, el liderazgo político y el deporte de élite mundial, el expresidente de Colombia, Álvaro Uribe Vélez, se reunió en España con Florentino Pérez, presidente del Real Madrid. La cita tuvo como propósito central articular alianzas de cooperación internacional enfocadas en la atención a las víctimas del reciente terremoto en Colombia y en el impulso de proyectos de desarrollo social para las poblaciones más vulnerables. El foco principal de las conversaciones entre ambas figuras estuvo en definir estrategias de apoyo directo para las comunidades golpeadas por la emergencia sísmica en el país. El plan contempla la canalización de recursos e iniciativas destinadas no solo a la respuesta inmediata frente a la tragedia, sino también a la reconstrucción del tejido social y a la generación de oportunidades sostenibles para la población infantil y juvenil de las zonas afectadas. Uno de los ejes más destacados del encuentro fue la propuesta de extender e implantar en el territorio colombiano academias vinculadas al Educational Football Program, una de las iniciativas bandera de la Fundación Real Madrid. Este modelo pedagógico y deportivo busca combinar el entrenamiento técnico del fútbol con la formación integral en valores humanos, tales como el trabajo en equipo, el respeto, la disciplina y la resiliencia. A través de estas escuelas socio-deportivas, se busca brindar a niños, niñas y jóvenes herramientas de prevención frente a la exclusión social y alternativas reales de desarrollo personal. El acercamiento y la logística de esta reunión internacional contaron con el acompañamiento y divulgación de la Fundación Revel, organización sin ánimo de lucro dedicada a la formación deportiva y educativa en la región iberoamericana. Directivos de esta entidad estuvieron presentes durante el diálogo, sirviendo como puente técnico para la futura implementación de los programas conjuntos en las regiones colombianas que más lo requieren. Con este acuerdo preliminar, se espera que en los próximos meses se concreten los cronogramas de llegada de las ayudas humanitarias y la apertura gradual de los centros deportivos y educativos de la mano de la Fundación Real Madrid y sus aliados locales.

articles.title: Hincha del Junior que fue discriminado por llevar chanclas fue obsequiado con un palco por un año
articles.standfirst: El joven seguidor ahorró peso a peso para conseguir su entrada
articles.summary: El joven seguidor ahorró peso a peso para conseguir su entrada
articles.body: Un caso de clasismo y rechazo en las tribunas del estadio terminó transformándose en una historia de solidaridad y premio al esfuerzo en Barranquilla. Germán, un joven fanático del Junior de Barranquilla que ahorró peso a peso para asistir al partido de su equipo, vivió un amargo momento que rápidamente despertó la indignación y la empatía en las redes sociales. Para Germán, asistir al partido del equipo rojiblanco contra el Deportivo Pereira no fue una decisión menor. Como estudiante, reunió con paciencia el dinero de sus meriendas diarias —ahorrando de $2.000 en $2.000 pesos— hasta lograr completar los $25.000 que costaba la boleta promocional para ingresar al escenario deportivo. Sin embargo, la alegría de alentar a su equipo se vio empañada por el rechazo. Una vez ubicado en la tribuna, una mujer se le acercó para increparlo y exigirle que se retirara del lugar debido a su calzado: llevaba puestas chancletas. A pesar de haber pagado legalmente su entrada, el joven prefirió evitar conflictos, aunque confesó sentirse dolido e incómodo por la situación. "No se debe juzgar a ninguna persona por la ropa que viste", reflexionó el aficionado tras el incidente. La historia se hizo viral en plataformas digitales, generando un masivo rechazo de la comunidad hacia la actitud discriminatoria vivida en las gradas. Entre las múltiples reacciones que provocó el caso, destacó la del empresario barranquillero Christian Daes, COO de la compañía Tecnoglass y conocido por su cercanía con la afición 'tiburona'. A través de su cuenta oficial en X (antes Twitter), Daes sentenció contundentemente: "Tiene palco asegurado para el otro año". Además, en tono jocoso para rechazar los prejuicios sociales, el empresario agregó que le encargaría calzado cómodo y que "no recibiría a nadie" en sus oficinas que no llegara en chancletas. El gesto de Daes no solo garantiza que el joven hincha pueda disfrutar de los partidos del Junior con la mejor comodidad durante las próximas temporadas, sino que también dejó una valiosa lección en la ciudad sobre la inclusión, el respeto y la pasión por el fútbol por encima de las apariencias.

articles.title: Dutch Darts Championship: Niels Zonneveld wins first senior PDC title with 8-5 victory over Danny Noppert in final
articles.summary: Niels Zonneveld defeated Danny Noppert 8-5 in the final of the Dutch Darts Championship; Zonneveld and Noppert beat Stephen Bunting and Gian van Veen in their respective semi-finals; watch Grand Slam of Darts live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
An entertaining all-Dutch final in Maastricht saw a tight contest with the score locked at 2-2 before Zonneveld won three successive legs to pull away.

Noppert responded to close the gap to 5-4 but Zonneveld regained control and won back-to-back legs - including a checkout of 157 - to earn a 7-4 lead.

Despite a tough battle against Noppert, Zonneveld was then able to see the match out with a 81 checkout, hitting double three to seal the title.

The 28-year-old's route to the final saw him beat Stephen Bunting 7-4 in the semi-finals and that match came following a stunning comeback with a final-leg 6-5 victory in the last eight. Up against Wessel Nijman, Zonneveld recovered from trailing 5-3 to level at 5-5 and was able to pounce after his fellow Dutchman missed a match dart.

Noppert also impressed in his run to the final, claiming a 7-5 win over compatriot Gian van Veen in the semi-finals to book his place in the tournament's showpiece.

It followed a comfortable quarter-final showing from Noppert, who recorded another impressive average on his way to reaching the last four, registering 113.42 in his 6-2 win over Luke Woodhouse.

In the quarter-finals, Bunting clinched a 6-3 win over Damon Heta and hit a 148 checkout, while Van Veen beat Ryan Searle 6-3.

Earlier on Sunday, round three provided some upsets as Gerwyn Price was beaten 6-4 by Zonneveld and Nathan Aspinall was thumped 6-1 by Bunting.

articles.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen and QB Daniel Jones were asked about fans booing; here's what they said
articles.summary: Colts were repeatedly booed by their fans in Sunday's 26-20 loss to Titans. Coach Shane Steichen: 'Don't blame them for booing one freaking bit'
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- The Colts were booed repeatedly in Sunday's embarrassing 26-20 loss to the Tennessee Titans, and neither coach Shane Steichen nor quarterback Daniel Jones had an issue with it.

"We've got to give them something to cheer about," Steichen said after his team blew a 13-0 halftime lead to the previously winless Titans on Sunday. "I don't blame them for booing one freaking bit."

Jones echoed his coach: "We didn't play well enough today. We've got to play better and give them something to cheer about. That's on us to play better."

There was also a brief "Fire Ball-ard" chant late in the game about, of course, general manager Chris Ballard, who is in his 10th season in charge of the organization.

Joel A. Erickson and Nathan Brown cover the Colts all season. Get more coverage on IndyStarTV and with the Colts Insider newsletter .

articles.title: Here is what Colts coach Shane Steichen said about his job security after loss to Titans
articles.summary: Colts coach Shane Steichen was asked about his job security after Sunday's 26-20 loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans; here's what he said
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- The Colts suffered a shocking 26-20 loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans on Sunday, blowing a 13-point halftime lead. Coach Shane Steichen brushed off questions about his job security after the game.

"Obviously, it's my job to get this team ready and that's what I'm focused on right now," he said after the game.

Steichen opened his postgame news conference by saying: "Extremely disappointing. We've got a lot to fix and we've got to fix it in a hurry."

When asked if he and team owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon had talked about his future, Steichen replied: "We haven't had those conversations. We just talk football."

articles.title: Todd Bowles replacements: Ranking Buccaneers' best candidates, from Mike Tomlin to Zac Taylor
articles.summary: As Todd Bowles' seat grows warmer, these coaching candidates could be options for the Buccaneers.
articles.body:
Most expected the Buccaneers to have a tough time getting past the Steelers with Baker Mayfield still out due to injury, but a blown 16-3 lead left Tampa Bay feeling the sting after Pittsburgh won in overtime.

That might not be the straw that breaks the camel's back for Todd Bowles' job security, but it only increases the heat on his seat as the Buccaneers drop to 1-5.

If Tampa Bay moves on from Bowles, who could fill his shoes on the Buccaneers' sideline?

1. Grant Udinski, Jaguars offensive coordinator

The Buccaneers probably wish Liam Coen, who was Bowles' offensive coordinator in 2024, was their head coach right now. They can't bring him back, but they can pry away his right-hand man.

Still only 30 years old, Grant Udinski seemingly had a real chance to be the Browns ' head coach this past offseason and was in the mix for the Bills ' job before sticking with Jacksonville. Trevor Lawrence has looked terrific early in the season, so Udinski's stock hasn't declined.

A Buccaneers team that seems likely to look for an offensive-minded coach could easily target Udinski and hope to pair him with an experienced defensive coordinator.

Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin walks off the field after his team fell 30-6 to the Houston Texans during the NFL Wild Card game at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh, PA on January 12, 2026. © Michael Longo/For USA Today Network-PA / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images

2. Mike Tomlin, former Steelers head coach

Will the Buccaneers just make Mike Tomlin say no? How in-demand the former Steelers coach will be remains to be seen, but it wouldn't hurt Tampa Bay (and other franchises) to gauge his interest.

As far as locations go for a coach who spent nearly two decades in Pittsburgh, Tampa Bay isn't too bad. Tomlin could pair good weather with a fairly well-run, low-drama organization in a perennially weak division by joining the Buccaneers. If reports are to be believed, though, Tomlin probably won't be ready to dive back into coaching this winter.

3. Nate Scheelhaase, Rams offensive coordinator

Nate Scheelhaase was another top candidate for the Browns this past season, and he's in his first season as the Rams ' offensive coordinator as Sean McVay's right-hand man. L.A.'s offense is starting to play well enough to keep Scheelhaase's stock high, and he seems to impress teams when he interviews.

After the Buccaneers cycled through offensive play-caller after offensive play-caller, does it make the most sense to give that role and head coaching duties to someone who isn't calling plays under McVay? If Scheelhaase's football mind is as impressive as teams believe, it could be worth a shot.

Sam Greene/The Enquirer / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images

The Bengals are intensely loyal to head coaches, bit what if they miss the playoffs again? Can they really run it back with Taylor for a ninth season? With pressure to win during Joe Burrow's prime, that scenario might necessitate a change.

Would the Buccaneers really go with a retread who had just been fired? Well, Taylor would take them out of the cycle of finding a new offensive play-caller each winter and give the franchise a coach who has been to a Super Bowl. With less competition in the division, a second act in Tampa Bay could be the right move for Taylor.

5. Klay Kubiak, 49ers offensive coordinator

Kubiak isn't the 49ers ' offensive play-caller, but the success of the Kyle Shanahan-Sean McVay tree is tough to deny. The son of Super Bowl-winning coach Gary Kubiak and Raiders coach Klint Kubiak, Klay appears to be next in line for a head coaching gig and could give the Buccaneers the kind of rising offensive mind they seem to need after so much offensive instability.

6. Anthony Campanile, Jaguars defensive coordinator

An offensive-minded coach seems to make the most sense for the Buccaneers, but if they really are looking to recapture some of the magic they found when Coen was on the staff, one of his understudies could make sense. If Udinski can't be pried away, could Jaguars DC Anthony Campanile be an option?

Campanile has impressed in his second season as a play-caller, and he received some interviews in the last cycle. If hired, though, Campanile would have to do what Bowles did and keep trying to find the right offensive play-caller.

articles.title: Cam Skattebo: I got punished for fumble and I understand why Giants did that
articles.summary: Skattebo barely played and never touched the ball on Sunday.
articles.body:
Giants running back Cam Skattebo only played a handful of snaps in Sunday's loss to the Saints and he never touched the ball, but head coach John Harbaugh said that wasn't by design and that Skattebo was not benched after losing a fumble in overtime of their Week 5 tie with the Commanders.

Skattebo had a somewhat different read on things. Skattebo said he "didn't expect to have zero" touches, but — as reported ahead of the game — that he was told that he would be seeing a sharp reduction in playing time.

"I got punished for what I did and I understand it ," Skattebo said, via Charlotte Carroll of TheAthletic.com. "I gotta be ready when coach calls my name and that wasn't today. . . . The message was keep your head down and keep going. They understand the type of player I am and I just gotta continue to do my job and do it to the best of my abilities."

Skattebo confirmed that the punishment was related to the fumble and reiterated that he accepts the team's decision.

"It's hard, but I've made mistakes and I got to own up to them," Skattebo said. "If that is what they want to do — keep me on the sidelines because of that — I totally understand. I can't make mistakes at this level of this game and when you make mistakes like that, consequences will be had."

The Giants got 34 yards on 14 carries by Tyrone Tracy, Devin Singletary and Najee Harris on Sunday, so they had to really stick to their guns to avoid looking Skattebo's way for an offensive spark that didn't come until J.J. McCarthy entered at quarterback with the Giants down 34-10 in the fourth quarter. We'll now wait to find out if Skattebo will get another shot against the Texans in Week 7.

articles.title: Report Card: Oregon Ducks 17, Huskers 14
articles.summary: Oops, they did it again. For those of you who stayed up to 1:45 am Sunday morning to watch THAT happen again, you are double struggling with a way-too early...
articles.body:
For those of you who stayed up to 1:45 am Sunday morning to watch THAT happen again, you are double struggling with a way-too early and a way-too often Nebraska pratfall, it's a doubly-painful Sunday.

In mid-August, Husker fans likely presumed Nebraska would be 5-2 at this point, and so Nebraska's record isn't the source of the pain. The pain is that Nebraska played well enough the first 50 minutes the last two weeks to be 7-0. Nebraska fans' glasses are more than half full, but it's starting to feel like filling it further is futile.

That futility justifiably leads to immense frustration, and that frustration results in irrational pessimism; it's the same pessimism that led Nebraska to replace not-winning-enough coaches with debacles like Bill Callahan and Mike Riley.

It's hard to argue that the same mental funk that fans are feeling isn't also present inside the program to some extent. This isn't the first time Nebraska has let a fourth quarter lead slip away. And if you watched ANY other college football in between naps, you know that this is the state of college football today.

It also doesn't help that the quarterback who we hoped would help break Nebraska of this had his fingers all over Oregon's comeback. But let's put Dylan Raiola's fourth quarter in perspective. Yes, Oregon scored 11 minutes in the final quarter, with Raiola leading two long touchdown drives. But let's not forget that Raiola did it in stereotypical Dylan fashion: 11 of 19 passes for 59 yards. Yes. 59 yards.

If there was a football program in this nation who knew what Dylan Raiola was going to do, it was the Nebraska Cornhuskers. Raiola was never going to test Nebraska's secondary; it was always going to be a horizontal passing game. Nebraska fans saw a green-tinged parody of the Husker offense from 2024 and 2025, yet for whatever reason, Nebraska never tried pressuring Raiola, unlike every other Big Ten team tries. Content, for whatever reason, to let Raiola have four to six yards every time he threw the ball.

I stayed up until TWO A.M. to watch THAT?

Yes, we should be mad and upset. But let's not overreact. If you had set the odds for the last two games in August, I suspect everyone would have have said the combined margins of victory for Indiana and Oregon around 30.

With that, it's onto the report card, and as always, your feedback is welcome in the comments.

QB : I went back and forth on how to grade Anthony Colandrea. He's one of the bigger reasons Nebraska was in this game, if only because he was able to make Duck Salad out of whatever Oregon threw at him. But he also missed too many opportunities and had too many mistakes. I'll grade him with a B- because I'm not sure he couldn't have put Nebraska in position to do more at the end of the game with more time.

I-Back : Mekhi Nelson's numbers didn't show it, but he probably had gained 30 yards after contact. There was simply no running room. Would have liked to have see Colandrea check down to backs in the flat; those were big plays earlier this season, and there were more than a couple of opportunities to do this Sunday morning. Isaiah Mozee's third quarter run was critical to getting Nebraska up 14-6. Jamal Rule must have reinjured himself; thank goodness a bye week is coming up. Grade: C+

WR : One of the things I hate about watching a Fox football broadcast is not seeing more of the game and the confused commentary. So when Devin Gardner insists that "nobody is open" and then I look at a snippet of a Fox replay and see that might not be the case, I'm going to err on the side of "Fox is wrong there too." I think there were plays to be made in the passing game, with the amount of pressure Oregon was committing up front. Grade: C+

OL : Oregon's defensive line owned this battle, and Nebraska never was able to get into a comfortable rhythm at anytime. Grade: D+

DL : On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's defensive line controlled Oregon's offensive line as well. At various times, Jahsear WHittington, Cam Lenhardt and Williams Nwaneri popped, thwarting the Ducks. Says a lot that the only time the Ducks offense had any success was going horizontal away from the line. Grade: A

LB: Huge game from Owen Chambliss (15 tackles) and Vincent Shavers (9 tackles). Grade: A

Secondary : Caleb Benning played huge, with 12 tackles filling in for Jamir Conn. Dwayne McDouble had a big interceptions and 13 tackles. But down the stretch, the secondary got singed by Raiola's dink-and-dunk game. It was death by 38 paper cuts in the fourth quarter. Grade: B

Special Teams: The special teams highlight was Archie Wilson's 60 yard punt midway through the fourth quarter. But then there were the lowlights: a low snap that Wilson had drop to a knee to field. I'm not going to criticize an Australian for not being as up on that bit of nuance to American football. Online, several media members seem to recognizing that Matt Rhule's disdain for fair catching kickoffs is costing Nebraska yards. 14 in this one, to be specific, and perhaps the only time it actually worked out on the second half opening kickoff. And while Nebraska never got close, you have to wonder how far downfield Colandrea had to get on the final drive to try a game-tying field goal attempt. I'm suspecting around the 20 personally. Grade: C+

Overall: B- Woulda, coulda, shoulda. Didn't. That's the bottom line. On a day where upsets were the rule, Nebraska couldn't avoid their own shadow.

articles.title: Footage shows ejected C.J. Gardner-Johnson crossing a gross line with Brock Bowers
articles.summary: What an unprofessional and immature display from the Bills' C.J. Gardner-Johnson.
articles.body:
C.J. Gardner-Johnson isn't exactly known for impeccable decision-making. There's a good reason the Buffalo Bills defensive back is on his fifth NFL team in the last few seasons , and it's not just because of his declining play as an "older" player (he's not even 30!).

We saw a first-hand example of Gardner-Johnson's evident lack of maturity during the Bills' game with the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. After getting caught arguing with Las Vegas star tight end Brock Bowers late in the first half, the officiating crew on hand decided to eject Gardner-Johnson from the proceedings. It was a bit of a confusing decision, considering no one understood exactly what happened during the tiff at first.

It turns out the officiating crew got it right. Replay footage showed Gardner-Johnson spitting on Raiders center Tyler Linderbaum during his unfriendly chat with Bowers. Yeah, that's going to earn an ejection every single time, folks. How gross and how immature all around:

There's showing physicality and playing with fire; then there's crossing a clear line of unnecessary disrespect. That's what Gardner-Johnson did by spitting on an opposing player. The Bills need a lot of the former. They need none of the latter. In all honesty, this is the sort of conduct that may well earn Gardner-Johnson a hefty fine, if not also a short one-game suspension.

Buffalo has a pivotal bye week coming up. It might have a decision on Gardner-Johnson's status moving forward, who is quickly proving to be more trouble than he's worth.

articles.title: Who won NASCAR Phoenix race? Winner is Tyler Reddick, plus full results

articles.body:
Tyler Reddick, who won the first three races of the 2026 season but hasn't won since April, claimed the NASCAR Phoenix race on Oct. 18 with only three races left in the Chase .

Reddick, in the No. 45 23XI Racing Toyota, capitalized on a late restart , moving from fifth to first to win his sixth race of the season in the Freeway Insurance 500 at Phoenix Raceway. He led only 18 laps.

Ryan Blaney, who led 51 laps and had won the previous two races at Phoenix, finished second; Chase Elliott was third, Christopher Bell was fourth, and Corey Heim was fifth.

articles.title: Jim Nantz injury: Did CBS broadcaster hurt his hand during Raiders-Bills?
articles.summary: CBS legend Jim Nantz might be playing through pain in the second half of Bills-Raiders
articles.body:
Including in the broadcast booth, apparently.

Late in the first half of Sunday's game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Buffalo Bills, analyst J.J. Watt and play-by-play legend Jim Nantz tried to demonstrate a "Peanut Punch," with Watt holding the football and Nantz applying the punch.

It apparently did not go well for Nantz:

"That was so much harder than I thought you were going to go," said Watt.

"My wrist is broken," reported Nantz after throwing the punch, as Watt asked for some ice for his broadcast partner. The broadcast then headed to a commercial break for the two-minute warning.

After the halftime break Nantz was back, with his wrist wrapped in the ice pack as Watt asked for:

As you can see, Nantz has his wrist wrapped and mentioned that there are "[g]onna be a few folks having to play hurt the last couple of quarters."

Including the broadcasting legend himself.

articles.title: Kyle Whittingham evaluates the ‘spark’ QB Tommy Carr brings to Michigan Football
articles.summary: Here’s what Kyle Whittingham had to say about Michigan QB Tommy Carr’s ‘spark’ of a performance versus Penn State.
articles.body:
With Bryce Underwood struggling against Penn State, Michigan made a quarterback change at halftime. Starting quarterback Bryce Underwood was 5-of-11 for 43 yards in the first half with two interceptions, and the offense had just 80 total yards. A spark was needed, Underwood was benched, and true freshman backup Tommy Carr was inserted.

Michigan's offense generated three touchdowns during Carr's half of action. In all, Carr was 5-of-7 for 47 yards, along with 36 rushing yards and a clutch 12-yard rushing score to put Michigan up at the time 21-11.

"He responded very well," Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham told the media . "It wasn't perfect. There's some things he obviously needs to get better at. But he had some key runs for us. That option there for that final touchdown. That was a great run."

Whittingham noted how Carr took care of the football and had no turnovers.

"He did a nice job. He's always prepared. I walk by that quarterback room 12 times, 15 times a day. He's in there pretty much every second he doesn't have class, Whittingham said, "He's in there watching film. He's very prepared when his number was called. And like I said, he responded very well. And going forward, we'll take a good hard look at the tape and see why things bogged down in the first half and why we were better in the second half because there really wasn't a lot of scheme change."

While Whittingham wouldn't announce whether Carr would be Michigan's QB1 versus Indiana, it would be a surprise if he wasn't after a strong showing in Michigan's come-from-behind win.

Carr, who stands 6-foot-4 and 195 pounds, may be a true freshman but was ready when his number was called. In fact, Carr's been ready for his time to shine for a while.

"I was prepared for this since week one," Carr said. "I prepared every day like I was the starter — got the call. There were a little bit of nerves, but I knew I was prepared and ready for this moment."

Michigan's offense needed a spark, Michigan's fanbase needed a spark, Michigan needed a change at quarterback for a fighting chance to turn the season around. If Carr is named Michigan's starting quarterback moving forward he'll have to deal with stiffer tests moving forward, including No. 6 Indiana next Saturday. The good news for Carr is Michigan's win over Penn State and his emergence as a potential difference-maker will have the fans rowdy when the Hoosiers come to town for a Big Noon kickoff on Fox.

articles.title: Week 6 Snap Reactions: Too little, too late
articles.summary: Atlanta’s late comeback can’t earn the win and can’t obscure all the team’s problems.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons made a late push, but ultimately couldn't overcome their early game errors and fell to 2-4 against the Chicago Bears.

The Falcons laundry list of injuries has brought down Jeff Ulbrich's house of cards. Fair to say he hasn't been on his A game, but you try to get your game off with Josh Woods, Mike Ford, Jared Ivey, etc. The hits keep coming; Kendal Daniels left after a frightening impact to the head and neck area. Divine Deablo continues to stack injuries and left with an arm injury, and Avieon Terrell and Billy Bowman were banged up late.

The defense needed the offense to carry them in this one, but their effort came too late.

Look, I'll fall on the sword after pounding the table for more Branch (even though I meant as a WR), but both returners attempted to field punts inside the 10; one couldn't read the ball well enough and muffed it, and the other forgot to fair catch. Almost like there's a reason most coaches don't let their guys attempt those at all. The mental mistakes are too numerous to blame solely on the players; they aren't getting good enough coaching.

This roster is packed with special teams talent, but it's not making a difference, and it's hard to ignore that the team hired two of the worst special teams coaches from 2025.

The late surge was great, but everything before it was embarrassing. Rees got in his own head in the first half and let the Bears dictate his run game. There's zero excuse for giving Bijan the ball 4 times in a half. His screen game needs to be trashed. After having no answers against pressure versus the Ravens, it took till the 4th quarter to get any against the Bears. Penix deserves a fair share of the blame when it comes to responding to pressure. He keeps locking in on his first read, and he has a bad habit of taking sacks and being careless with the football.

Kyle Pitts continues to have his talents wasted. He's one of the team's best answers against pressure and makes things happen when he gets the ball, but even after the team prioritized him this offseason, he's still an afterthought.

The Falcons have two 2-game losing streaks and one 2-game winning streak–they're streaky. After praising Stefanski and Co. for resetting the team after a Cooper Rush-led start, they've since failed to wash away concerns about this team's ability to play competent football week to week and quarter to quarter.

The Bears aren't a cakewalk, but their defense isn't an immovable object; the Falcons late surge proved that. Even when the Falcons were spotted over 100 penalty yards, they looked inept for most of the game. Mental mistakes showed up in every phase of the game, and the staff failed to give the players a viable game plan.

The Atlanta Falcons are now two games below .500 as they enter the rough patch of their schedule. There's plenty of blame to go around, and the team better get itself sorted quickly because the 49ers are up next, and Kyle Shanahan and Raheem Morris are licking their chops.

articles.title: Badgers grades, snap counts on defense from Week 7 vs. UCLA: Did the defense actually play poorly?
articles.summary: How did the Badgers fare on Saturday?
articles.body:
The Wisconsin Badgers fell to the UCLA Bruins 17-7 on Saturday evening, missing an opportunity to upset a ranked opponent. Instead, they remained out of the AP Top 25 on Sunday, while the Bruins moved up to No. 9 in the country.

While Wisconsin's offense really struggled, the Badgers defense did a great job in one key category: defending the run. Wisconsin held star running back Wayne Knight to just 23 yards on 13 carries, and the Badgers really forced UCLA to get everything in the air until the final drive when the game was out of hand.

The pass defense is where the Badgers struggled. Wisconsin allowed UCLA to convert 13 third downs and hold the ball for over 37 minutes of clock, as they just could not get off the field.

Here are the snap counts and PFF grades for the defense from Wisconsin's loss to UCLA on Saturday.

Hammond Russell IV – Snap Count: [42], Grade: 56.6

Charles Perkins – Snap Count: [27], Grade: 62.3

Junior Poyser – Snap Count: [25], Grade: 77.2

DeNigel Cooper – Snap Count: [20], Grade: 50.8

Nolan Vils – Snap Count: [19], Grade: 67.9

Dillan Johnson – Snap Count: [9], Grade: 49.8

Michael Garner – Snap Count: [9], Grade: 48.2

Jacob Anderson – Snap Count: [1], Grade: 60.0

Hammond Russell played the most snaps for the Badgers, but they rotated a ton of bodies as they have all season. Really, for the most part, this group did their job. Wisconsin came into this game looking to stop the run, which meant winning the line of scrimmage, and they did that.

Junior Poyser was the player who stood out the most of this group in live time. On a game with over 75 defensive plays, he got a good number of snaps.

Sebastian Cheeks – Snap Count: [58], Grade: 67.7

Tyreese Fearbry – Snap Count: [45], Grade: 71.3

Justus Boone – Snap Count: [26], Grade: 66.8

Nicolas Clayton – Snap Count: [25], Grade: 50.6

Aaron Witt – Snap Count: [14], Grade: 62.0

Sebastian Cheeks, who has been one of the best pass rushers in the country, saw a ton of chips from UCLA. Still, Wisconsin had 21 pressures, as Mike Tressel looked to blitz Ty Dieffenbach a good amount.

Many, including Luke Fickell, didn't think the Badgers got enough pressure on the quarterback in this one. To me, they honestly were winning at the line of scrimmage throughout the game. Dieffenbach just made some really nice plays early under pressure, and UCLA had a great game plan to get the ball out of his hands quickly, especially when the blitz was sent.

Dieffenbach was pressured on 16 of his 33 dropbacks. For reference, Colton Joseph was pressured on 11 of his 21, while Dieffenbach had a much quicker time to throw.

Nicolas Clayton had the best game of his career to date. He had five pressures, while Cheeks still got three despite the extra attention.

Mason Posa – Snap Count: [77], Grade: 77.6

Cooper Catalano – Snap Count: [77], Grade: 63.5

Jon Jon Kamara – Snap Count: [3], Grade: 59.9

Wisconsin looked to blitz a ton on this one, and Mason Posa ended up with five pressures. Posa ended up being all over the field in this one. While he was targeted a few times in coverage, Posa had seven tackles and six defensive stops. He was also quite disruptive as a pass-rusher, adding a team-high five pressures.

Catalano had five tackles, three defensive stops, two pressures, and a key pass breakup. Both of these players had solid games with a few missed plays.

Jai'mier Scott – Snap Count: [70], Grade: 63.3

Bryce West – Snap Count: [59], Grade: 66.9

Javan Robinson – Snap Count: [55], Grade: 67.9

Eric Fletcher Jr. – Snap Count: [26], Grade: 61.8

Wisconsin rotated in Eric Fletcher Jr. with Javan Robinson in this game, so there may have been a potential injury there. But Robinson remained lockdown on his side of the field, as he wasn't targeted once.

I was impressed by Jai'mier Scott as well, as I thought he had a few very good coverage reps, and he made a few open-field tackles as well.

The Bruins looked to work in the short and intermediate range over the middle of the field, and Bryce West was heavily targeted. He gave up seven catches on nine targets, giving up 85 receiving yards.

Matthew Jung – Snap Count: [63], Grade: 68.1

Marvin Burks Jr. – Snap Count: [46], Grade: 69.7

Cairo Skanes – Snap Count: [37], Grade: 65.0

Matthew Traynor – Snap Count: [10], Grade: 68.2

Carson Van Dinter – Snap Count: [4], Grade: 62.0

Matt Jung played a majority of the game, but was ejected late in the fourth quarter on a targeting call. I thought this group struggled in coverage a bit. Jung had a costly mistake on a third and long, as he came down off his receiver as Ty Dieffenbach scrambled to extend a play. The Bruins ended up converting the play and extended the drive.

It felt like UCLA was also consistently looking around Cairo Skanes when he was on the field. Skanes was credit with two receptions allowed for 24 yards, but he had a late coverage bust that led to a game-sealing explosive for UCLA, and it also looked like he also had some communication issues in coverage.

Still, the defense only gave up 17 points and was able to stop the run at a high level, so there are definitely some things to build off from the loss.

articles.title: Kendre Miller productive in Week 6
articles.summary: Saints RB Kendre Miller receives team-high 20 carries in Week 6 and posts 70 yards
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints RB Kendre Miller rushed for 70 yards on 20 carries against the New York Giants in Week 6.
