articles.title: Dillon's goal lifts No. 1 Fort Hill in regular-season finale
articles.summary: CUMBERLAND — No. 1 Fort Hill and No. 5 Lighthouse Christian played a tight, defensive battle in the schools’ first-ever meeting. But all it took was a slight...
articles.body:
CUMBERLAND — No. 1 Fort Hill and No. 5 Lighthouse Christian played a tight, defensive battle in the schools' first-ever meeting.

But all it took was a slight defensive lapse from the Seahawks to put the Sentinels on top.

Jaiden Dillon scored a goal late in the first half off a throw-in to send Fort Hill to a 1-0 victory over Lighthouse on Saturday afternoon at Greenway Avenue Stadium.

Saturday marked the end of the regular season for both teams.

Fort Hill claimed its 12th consecutive win to improve to 13-1. Lighthouse dropped its second straight contest for a 21-3-1 record.

"We knew we were gonna be in for a fight," Fort Hill coach Zach Steckman said. "It was a good battle. Lighthouse's got a great team. They had a great game plan to kind of slow us down a little bit, and we broke through that one time."

It took both teams a bit to find their footing, as neither squad recorded a shot on goal during the opening 10 minutes.

The first scoring chance for either side came on a Fort Hill corner kick around the 26:15 mark. John Reinhardt tried to head the kick into the net, but it hit the post for a Seahawks goal kick.

After that, both teams took cracks at the net, but goalies Bobby Brauer of Fort Hill and Peyton Poland of Lighthouse did everything they could to keep it a scoreless contest.

The Sentinels were awarded a throw-in on the Seahawks' defensive third. Hunter Nyland heaved it towards the box where Hunter Raines fired the initial shot.

Raines' attempt then ricocheted off Dillon's head and into the net for the game's only goal at the 4:14 mark.

"That goal in the moment was huge for us," Steckman said. "Jaiden's a spark plug kind of guy. He works his tail off for us and gives 100% effort all the time.

"It seems that every time we get him in there, something happens, whether he's scoring a goal or making a hustle play, defensive play, whatever."

The physicality continued into the second half as Fort Hill was assessed two yellow cards during the period.

The Seahawks attempted three free kicks during the second half, but couldn't place them into the net.

Lighthouse's best one came off the foot of Elijah Ziler with about 9:15 left to play, but Brauer punched it out.

The Seahawks' other two free kicks sailed out of bounds.

Fort Hill finished with significant advantages in shots (12-6) and corners (5-1).

Brauer made five saves for the Sentinels' eighth shutout of the season.

The Sentinels' backline made things difficult for the area's all-time leading scorer Sammy Scritchfield, who came into Saturday's contest with 43 goals on the season and 151 for his career.

"We think we have the best defense in the area (and the) best goalie in the area," Steckman said. "We get that one goal, or however many goals it takes, and those guys lock it down."

Poland stopped eight shots for the Seahawks, who were held scoreless for just the second time this season.

"They put it in, we didn't stop it, and that's part of the game," Lighthouse coach David Ziler said. "We got young guys in there playing, I mean my backline has ninth graders on it. And you're competing against the best team in the area, I think we did fine."

Fort Hill will have an extended break before competing in the Class A West Region playoffs.

Lighthouse qualified as the No. 2 seed for the Maryland State Christian School tournament and will host Greater Grace Christian in the first round on Tuesday at 4:30 p.m.

Lighthouse defeated Greater Grace in penalty kicks during a regular-season tournament last month.

The winner will take on either No. 3 seed Rockbridge Academy or No. 6 Southern Maryland Christian in Thursday's semifinal round.

"This is a tough team," David Ziler said about Fort Hill. "So if we can compete here, then hopefully we can compete in all levels of our state playoffs that we're going to be in and our national run that we're going to try to make."

articles.title: No. 1 Fort Hill, No. 2 Frankfort win big
articles.summary: HAGERSTOWN — No. 1 Fort Hill ran all over North Hagerstown in a 42-6 rout on Friday night. The undefeated Sentinels (7-0) accumulated 387 yards rushing as a...
articles.body:
HAGERSTOWN — No. 1 Fort Hill ran all over North Hagerstown in a 42-6 rout on Friday night.

The undefeated Sentinels (7-0) accumulated 387 yards rushing as a team. Neek Taylor led the rushing attack with 137 yards and scored once.

Carson Bender added 127 yards and three scores on the ground.

Bender scored his first touchdown on an opening drive that covered 61 yards in seven plays.

The Hubs (3-4) responded on their opening possession. Quarterback Ronnie Savage found Michael Stewart for 52 yards to put the ball at the Sentinels 8.

Two plays later, Stewart plunged into the end zone from one yard out.

The Hubs' two-point attempt was unsuccessful, so Fort Hill hung onto a 7-6 lead.

From that point on, however, it was Fort Hill. The Sentinels ended the game with 35 unanswered points.

Channing Logsdon and Levi House also found the end zone. Logsdon scored on a 17-yard run in the third quarter.

House intercepted a Savage pass and returned it 45 yards to the house for the game's final touchdown.

The sophomore middle linebacker also served as the Sentinels' starting quarterback in place of an injured Brady O'Neal.

Despite the win, Fort Hill committed 16 penalties.

Fort Hill will travel to Smithsburg for battle of undefeated squads on Friday at 6 p.m.

SHORT GAP, W.Va. — Eleven players helped No. 2 Frankfort churn 210 yards on the ground for a 41-6 win over Petersburg.

The Falcons extended their area record to 35 consecutive victories.

Cole Shanholtz led the ground game with 45 yards on five attempts.

Jake Snurr added 26 yards on four carries and scored a touchdown on each side of the ball. He returned a 35-yard scoop-and-score nearly halfway through the second quarter.

Bradyn Tyler, Gunnar Bradshaw and Christian Hyett also scored on offense.

Brady Twigg returned an interception 21 yards to the house in the first quarter.

Frankfort led 34-0 at halftime and played many of its reserves in the second half.

Backup quarterback Carson McBee completed two passes for a total of 42 yards.

One of those completions was to Knox Kelly for 24 yards, while Matthew Iser hauled in an 18-yard reception.

Peyton Brittingham led the Falcons' defense with five tackles, including two that went for a loss, and an interception.

Vikings running back Micah Ertel scored the only touchdown for Petersburg (2-5) in the fourth quarter.

Frankfort will face fellow undefeated squad Wahama on the road Saturday at 1:30 p.m.

articles.title: Inside Greg Luca's AP Top 25 ballot: Sorting through an unprecedented week
articles.summary: Criticism of the latest AP Top 25 was every bit as loud as expected after a wild weekend that left voters scrambling to make sense of the rankings.
articles.body:
After a week of record-setting turmoil at the top of the rankings, the only guarantee was outrage.

Five of the top seven teams in the AP Top 25 lost on the same day for the first time in the poll's history, leaving the voters to sort through a jumbled pile of contradictory results and conflicting resumes. Even if all 70 ballots made sense independently, the final tally after mashing them together was always destined to be flawed.

Difference from poll results in parentheses

Through each week of my debut season with an AP Top 25 ballot , we'll take you inside my thought process behind the picks, looking this week at some of the loudest criticisms from the year's most controversial set of rankings.

The poor optics jumped off the page the moment the poll was released. One day after Florida beat Texas 27-24 in Austin, the Gators checked in at No. 20, one spot behind the No. 19 Longhorns.

Again, the poll results come from a points tally. The AP voters did not have a committee meeting that ended with an agreement to flout the previous day's head-to-head.

My ballot was one of the most polarized in this regard, as I had Texas at No. 16 while leaving Florida unranked.

The Longhorns' body of work still presents a strong overall case. Texas has wins over No. 3 Ohio State and No. 11 Tennessee, and the Longhorns still rank eighth in SP+ efficiency and ninth in adjusted EPA per play .

The ugly nature of Texas' 27-24 losses to Florida and Oklahoma hurts in the eye test, but analytics tell a different story. Per postgame win expectancy data from ESPN's Bill Connelly , the Longhorns had just a 1.2% chance of going 0-2 against the Gators and Sooners the past two weeks. In other words, Texas built the types of statistical edges that usually lead to wins, suggesting the outcomes were more likely to be flukes than indicators of the Longhorns' downfall.

Texas' close final margins also inspire more confidence than Florida's 45-17 loss to Missouri on Oct. 3 and last week's 38-19 home loss to a South Carolina team that appeared to be on the verge of firing its coach.

The Gators are much worse than the Longhorns in the analytics - No. 38 in SP+ and No. 29 in adjusted EPA per play - and Florida's inconsistency is too alarming to merit a top-25 spot.

Why is Georgia ranked ahead of Tennessee?

Before Saturday's shocking home loss to Auburn, Georgia was the best and most consistent team in the nation. The Bulldogs won their first five games by at least 24 points, then beat Alabama 20-17 on the road last week to mark one of the most impressive results for any team this season.

The counterargument is obvious: Tennessee was even more impressive in a 26-10 win against that same Alabama team Saturday, delivering a smothering defensive performance.

But one solid showing from quarterback George MacIntyre isn't enough to undo concerns about a Tennessee offense that has struggled most of the year, narrowly defeating lowly Arkansas a week ago.

The combination of quarterback Gunner Stockton and coach Kirby Smart at the head of one of the nation's most reliable programs is still easier to trust going forward, and the Bulldogs checked in at No. 2 in SP+ even with Saturday's loss.

My No. 6 ranking for Georgia was one spot lower than the AP average, while my No. 9 ranking for Tennessee was two spots higher than the consensus. But I do agree that they belong in that order.

Notre Dame's soft schedule makes the Fighting Irish an easy target, and many fans wanted to see a steeper drop after Saturday's 28-24 loss at BYU.

But in a hostile primetime environment against a Cougars team that now ranks No. 2 in the country, the Fighting Irish played to a near stalemate . Notre Dame and BYU both finished with 0.10 EPA per play for the game, and the Cougars' 45% success rate just edged the 44% success rate for the Fighting Irish.

Notre Dame also remains strong in the yearlong analytics despite facing lesser competition, sitting No. 4 in SP+ and No. 2 in adjusted EPA per play.

Given that Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin will be out "several weeks" due to injury, according to coach Ryan Day, a case exists to keep Notre Dame at No. 3, bumping Ohio State to No. 4. But I chose to reward Ohio State for Saturday's 19-15 win at Indiana and a strong analytics profile, keeping the Buckeyes at No. 3 while slotting the Fighting Irish at No. 4.

articles.title: Steelers mount incredible 4th quarter comeback against the Buccaneers
articles.summary: It looked as if an unfortunate trend would continue for the Steelers on Sunday. And then, the improbably occurred.
articles.body:
As the Steelers entered Week 6 of the NFL season, they had yet to win consecutive games on the season. A Week 1 victory was followed by a loss, and then a Week 3 victory was also followed by a loss. So when the Steelers won last week, and were trailing by 13 points at the start of their showdown with the Buccaneers on Sunday, it seemed as if an unfortunate trend would continue for Pittsburgh.

But the Steelers were far from quitting, and a lot can happen in 15 minutes – even enough to score 16 points and force an overtime match-up. And that's exactly what happened, as Pittsburgh managed a rally led by a pair of veteran presences that would end up leading to a 26-19 victory in overtime to grace head coach Mike McCarthy with his first back-to-back wins since taking over as the franchise's head coach.

Aaron Rodgers, Chris Boswell power late Steelers rally

The comeback began early in the fourth quarter, with the Steelers trailing 16-3. Aaron Rodgers moved the ball downfield and connected on a 5-yard touchdown pass to bring the Steelers within one score, with a Chris Boswell PAT narrowing Tampa Bay's lead to six points.

Boswell would end up being the star for the rest of the fourth quarter. Rodgers did enough to get the team into field goal position on three straight drives to close out regulation, and Boswell would subsequently boot a 39-yard field goal, a 58-yard field goal, and a 20-yard field goal to put the Steelers ahead by three points with just over a minute left to play.

Unfortunately for the Steelers, the Buccaneers would drive down the field to tie up the game and force overtime. But fortunately for the Steelers, they had Rodgers at quarterback, as he engineered another touchdown drive in overtime, capped off by a 6-yard touchdown pass. On the ensuing drive, the Steelers defense would bring the game to a close.

Boswell set the franchise record for most field goals on Sunday after converting four total in the win, while Rodgers would finish the day 33-for-49 with 253 yards and two touchdowns.

articles.title: Panthers TE Tommy Tremble speaks on his knockout of a TD celebration in Week 6
articles.summary: Panthers TE Tommy Tremble delivered two knockout punches in front of the Philadelphia crowd on Sunday.
articles.body:
For most of those who were involved, today's victory for the Carolina Panthers over the Philadelphia Eagles will be a forgettable one. The sloppy triumph included a backup quarterback, a fourth-string running back, a dozen injury-related timeouts and a combined 24 penalties for a total of 233 yards lost.

But among all the ugly was a pretty performance from Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble, who posted four catches, 46 yards and—for the first time in his six-year NFL career—two touchdowns.

articles.title: Twitter reacts to A.J. Brown's drops, Patriots close win over Jets
articles.summary: It wasn't perfect by any stretch, but the Patriots escaped a tough divisional game against the Jets on Sunday.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots held on for a 26-19 victory over the New York Jets at Gillette Stadium on Sunday.

It was a physical game that was hard-fought for the Patriots on both sides of the ball. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye was efficient all afternoon, going 18-of-32 passing for 235 yards and three touchdowns.

However, one of the surprise heroes of the game was running back Corey Kiner, who led the ground game with 57 yards on 11 carries. That includes a late fourth-quarter drive where Kiner essentially helped put the game out of reach.

A.J. Brown made his return for the game, but he only caught three passes for 27 yards, while also racking up three drops. It wasn't the best performance from the three-time All-Pro wide receiver by any stretch, but he was clearly dealing with some rust after missing the previous four games.

On the defensive side of the ball, the Patriots did enough to force field goals and the first interception thrown by Jets quarterback Geno Smith.

articles.title: Alvin Kamara posts 69 total yards and one TD
articles.summary: Saints RB Alvin Kamara involved in running and passing game in Week 6 win
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints RB Alvin Kamara rushed for 34 yards on seven carries against the New York Giants in Week 6. He also caught two passes for 35 yards and one touchdown during the game.

Why It Matters: It appears like Kamara is back to being a weapon in the running and passing game but is not receiving most of the carries during games. He should see a decent amount of touches next week and can be a No. 3 receiver or flex option in leagues.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy: I got stepped on before halftime, team adjusted well without me
articles.summary: The sideline medical tents in the NFL are in place for players, but they're ocassionally needed for others over the course of a game and that was the case in...
articles.body:
The sideline medical tents in the NFL are in place for players, but they're ocassionally needed for others over the course of a game and that was the case in Tampa on Sunday.

While the Steelers went into the locker room at halftime, head coach Mike McCarthy remained on the field and went to the tent. The CBS broadcast said that McCarthy was undergoing treatment for an ankle injury and McCarthy said at his postgame press conference that he was hurt when he got stepped on during the first half.

The Steelers trailed 13-3 at the break, but took the game to overtime and then won on Aaron Rodgers's touchdown pass to wide receiver Germie Bernard in the extra period.

"They didn't miss a beat," McCarthy said. "Adjustments were made, and halftime's quick, anyway. Frankly, the the biggest part was really just getting the offensive conversations to me when when the guys came out. I thought the guys did what they needed to do."

McCarthy and the Steelers will now head to France to face the Saints and the coach will be hoping to avoid any trips to the tent on that side of the Atlantic.
